A co-expression module is a group of proteins whose abundances rise and fall together across
biopsies. WGCNA (Langfelder and Horvath 2008) finds them, and each module is then summarised by
its eigengene: one number per biopsy that follows the module's shared pattern. Later steps test
eigengenes instead of hundreds of single proteins. Module construction never sees a group label or
a phenotype.

## Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(WGCNA)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "analysis_reporting_helpers.R"))
disableWGCNAThreads()
```

## Input

limpa's complete matrix with each protein's blood slope removed. WGCNA takes no covariate and no
missing values, so this is the matrix it can use. It inherits the blood-removal problem shown in
`03_Quantification` for the 85 proteins measured in 20 or fewer runs.

```{r}
#| label: input
stage <- here("01_Processing", "06_Module_Building")
out <- file.path(stage, "c_data")
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
inputs <- c(corrected = "01_Processing/03_Quantification/c_data/DAList_corrected.rds")
paths <- map_chr(inputs, here)
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
corrected <- readRDS(paths[["corrected"]])
abund <- as.matrix(corrected$data)
meta <- as_tibble(corrected$metadata) |>
  select(sample_id, subject, group, timepoint)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(abund), meta$sample_id))
dim(abund)
count(count(meta, subject, name = "biopsies"), biopsies, name = "people")
```

## Define modules on within-person variation

WGCNA treats every biopsy as an independent sample. These 45 biopsies come from 16 people
measured up to three times, and person identity drives the leading components of the abundance
matrix. Left alone, modules would mostly group proteins that differ between people. So the
modules are defined on person-centred abundance: each protein's value minus that person's mean.
A person with a single biopsy centres to zeros and adds nothing, so they are left out of the
definition and kept for scoring.

```{r}
#| label: centre
repeated <- meta |>
  add_count(subject) |>
  filter(n > 1)
centred <- t(apply(abund[, repeated$sample_id], 1, \(x) x - ave(x, repeated$subject)))
expr <- t(centred)
one <- repeated$sample_id[repeated$subject == repeated$subject[1]]
rbind(raw = round(abund[1, one], 2), centred = round(centred[1, one], 2))
c(runs_defining = nrow(expr), runs_scored = ncol(abund))
```

## Soft power

WGCNA turns each pair's correlation into a connection strength by raising it to a power (the soft
power): higher powers keep strong links and shrink weak ones. The chosen power is the lowest whose
network looks scale-free, meaning a few proteins carry many connections and most carry few, by a
fit R² of at least 0.85 (`pickSoftThreshold()`'s estimate). The WGCNA FAQ's table for signed
networks (12 for over 40 samples) is the fallback if no power reaches it.

Two settings depart from the package defaults, both recommended in the WGCNA FAQ:

- a signed network, so proteins that move in opposite directions are not linked;
- biweight midcorrelation (bicor), a correlation that down-weights outlying values, with
  `maxPOutliers = 0.05` (the default of 1 switches that guard off). `pearsonFallback` uses an
  ordinary correlation for a protein with zero spread.

```{r}
#| label: soft-power
bicor_args <- list(corType = "bicor", maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = "individual")
sft <- pickSoftThreshold(expr,
  powerVector = 1:20, networkType = "signed",
  corFnc = "bicor", corOptions = list(maxPOutliers = 0.05), verbose = 0
)
faq_power <- c(18L, 16L, 14L, 12L)[findInterval(nrow(expr), c(20, 31, 41)) + 1]
power <- coalesce(sft$powerEstimate, faq_power)
fit_indices <- as_tibble(sft$fitIndices) |>
  mutate(signed_r2 = -sign(slope) * SFT.R.sq, chosen = Power == power)
filter(fit_indices, Power %in% (power + -2:2)) |>
  select(Power, signed_r2, mean.k., chosen)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-soft-power
#| fig-cap: "Connectivity and signed scale-free fit by soft power; dashed 0.85, red chosen."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.5
fit_indices |>
  select(Power, `signed scale-free R2` = signed_r2, `mean connectivity` = mean.k.) |>
  pivot_longer(-Power) |>
  ggplot(aes(Power, value)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = Power == power), size = 2) +
  geom_hline(
    data = tibble(name = "signed scale-free R2", y = 0.85), aes(yintercept = y),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey30", `TRUE` = "#B2182B"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "soft power", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

## Modules

`blockwiseModules()` builds the network, measures how many neighbours each pair shares (the
topological overlap, TOM), clusters proteins on it, and merges modules whose eigengenes correlate
above 0.85 (`mergeCutHeight = 0.15`). Proteins that fit no module go to `grey`. Settings that are
not package defaults: `minModuleSize = 30` (default `min(20, n/2)`; no recorded evidence for 30)
and `maxBlockSize = 2500`, which keeps all 1,900 proteins in one block. `randomSeed` seeds the
clustering inside the function; a `set.seed()` outside it would be overridden.

```{r}
#| label: modules
net <- do.call(blockwiseModules, c(
  list(expr,
    power = power, networkType = "signed", TOMType = "signed",
    deepSplit = 2, minModuleSize = 30, mergeCutHeight = 0.15,
    pamStage = TRUE, pamRespectsDendro = TRUE, maxBlockSize = 2500,
    numericLabels = FALSE, randomSeed = 54321, verbose = 0
  ),
  bicor_args
))
colours <- set_names(net$colors, colnames(expr))
sort(table(colours), decreasing = TRUE)
```

## Eigengenes and membership

The eigengene is the first principal component of a module's proteins, scored here on the
uncentred matrix so that differences between people, and so between HR and LR, stay testable.
`moduleEigengenes()` flips each eigengene's sign to follow the module's average abundance (package
default).

```{r}
#| label: eigengenes
me <- moduleEigengenes(t(abund), colors = colours, excludeGrey = TRUE)$eigengenes
rownames(me) <- colnames(abund)
eigengenes <- t(as.matrix(me))
rownames(eigengenes) <- sub("^ME", "", rownames(eigengenes))
round(eigengenes[1:3, 1:4], 3)
```

A protein's kME is its correlation with its module's eigengene: near 1 means it follows the module
closely. kME is read on the person-centred data that defined the modules, because on uncentred
data the differences between people dilute it.

```{r}
#| label: kme
centred_me <- moduleEigengenes(expr, colors = colours, excludeGrey = TRUE)$eigengenes
kme <- signedKME(expr, centred_me,
  corFnc = "bicor", corOptions = "maxPOutliers = 0.05, pearsonFallback = 'individual'"
)
colnames(kme) <- sub("^kME", "", colnames(kme))
gene_of <- set_names(corrected$annotation$gene, corrected$annotation$uniprot_id)
membership <- tibble(
  uniprot_id = names(colours), gene = unname(gene_of[names(colours)]), module = unname(colours)
) |>
  mutate(kme = map2_dbl(uniprot_id, module, \(id, m) if (m == "grey") NA_real_ else kme[id, m]))
membership |>
  filter(module != "grey") |>
  slice_max(kme, n = 2, by = module) |>
  arrange(module) |>
  head(6)
```

## How much each eigengene still depends on the person

The intraclass correlation (ICC) is the share of an eigengene's variance that lies between people
rather than between one person's biopsies, from a mixed model with time point fitted (lme4,
`eigengene ~ timepoint + (1 | subject)`), so time effects do not count as noise.

```{r}
#| label: icc
eigengene_long <- as_tibble(t(eigengenes), rownames = "sample_id") |>
  pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "module", values_to = "eigengene") |>
  left_join(meta, by = "sample_id")
subject_icc <- eigengene_long |>
  summarise(
    icc = {
      v <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(suppressMessages(
        lme4::lmer(eigengene ~ timepoint + (1 | subject))
      )))$vcov
      v[1] / (v[1] + v[2])
    },
    .by = module
  )
module_summary <- count(filter(membership, module != "grey"), module, name = "n_proteins") |>
  left_join(subject_icc, by = "module") |>
  arrange(desc(n_proteins))
module_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sizes
#| fig-cap: "Proteins per module, labelled with the eigengene's person ICC."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5
module_colours <- set_names(module_summary$module, module_summary$module)
module_summary |>
  mutate(module = factor(module, levels = rev(module))) |>
  ggplot(aes(n_proteins, module, fill = module)) +
  geom_col(colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("ICC %.2f", icc)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = module_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(x = "proteins", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-trajectories
#| fig-cap: "Eigengene per biopsy. Thin lines: one person. Thick line and range: group mean ± SE."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6
trajectory <- eigengene_long |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(eigengene), se = sd(eigengene) / sqrt(n()),
    .by = c(module, group, timepoint)
  )
ggplot(trajectory, aes(timepoint, mean, colour = group, group = group)) +
  geom_line(
    data = eigengene_long, aes(y = eigengene, group = subject),
    alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), size = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(module, levels = module_summary$module), nrow = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(HR = "#2166AC", LR = "#B2182B"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "eigengene") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  identical(colnames(eigengenes), meta$sample_id),
  setequal(rownames(eigengenes), setdiff(unique(colours), "grey")),
  all(abs(membership$kme[membership$module != "grey"]) <= 1),
  sum(module_summary$n_proteins) + sum(colours == "grey") == nrow(abund)
)
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: summary
at_power <- filter(fit_indices, Power == power)
```

Soft power `r power` (signed R² `r round(at_power$signed_r2, 3)`, mean connectivity
`r round(at_power$mean.k., 1)`). `r nrow(eigengenes)` modules of `r min(module_summary$n_proteins)`
to `r max(module_summary$n_proteins)` proteins; `r sum(colours == "grey")` of `r length(colours)`
proteins fit no module. `r nrow(expr)` of `r ncol(abund)` runs defined the modules. Module colours
are labels only and change if `01_Processing` is rebuilt.

## Save

`modules.rds` is read by module characterisation, module contrasts and preservation,
classification, the trait steps, proteome clustering and the F2 figure.

```{r}
#| label: save
saveRDS(
  list(
    eigengenes = eigengenes, membership = membership, meta = meta, module_summary = module_summary
  ),
  file.path(out, "modules.rds"),
  compress = "xz"
)
sheets <- list(
  module_summary = module_summary, membership = membership,
  eigengenes = as_tibble(t(eigengenes), rownames = "sample_id"),
  soft_threshold = fit_indices
)
holds <- c(
  "Proteins per module and the subject ICC of its eigengene.",
  "Every protein's module and its kME in that module.",
  "Module eigengene per sample, scored on raw abundance.",
  "pickSoftThreshold fit indices per power; chosen marks the power used."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "module_building.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
```
